newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Share row unlikely to damage govt - Howard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Share row unlikely to damage govt - Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the intensifying share row was unlikely to do any major damage to the government in the long term.

"I'm very sorry for what's occurred over the last week, but it hasn't involved any wrongdoing or Any cheating or dishonesty and I think that's what will register with thE Australian public," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Allegations of conflicts of interest over the ownership of shares have cost Howard two government members this week and the opposition is currently targeting another three ovEr the same issue.
Howard said he did not know whether the controversy would harm the government's chances of retaining the federal seat of Lindsay in the by-election there this Saturday.

"It's very difficult to know whether those issues have much of an impact out in the electorate because the electorate's pretty smart," he said. "I really don't know and I think we'll just know on Saturday night."

The share affair erupted last week when the opposition accused Assistant Treasurer Jim Short of breaching Howard's ministerial guidelines by making a decision regarding a company in which he held shares.
Short resigned over the issue on Sunday and was followed by Senator Brian Gibson, who resigned as parliamentary secretary to the treasurer on Tuesday as a result of a similar incident.
The opposition is now targeting Industry Minister John Moore, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer and Finance Minister John Fahey, saying they have also breached the guidelines.
Under the guidelines, government members are required to divest any investments which may conflict with their portfolio area.
Howard has said the guidelines may be too strict and should be reviewed. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273 2730
